deep.reconstruction:
This page is a heavily corrected pencil draft of the opening sections of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), roughly Abtheilung I, §§3–5. It is written over a printed postal/expense form headed 'No 10.' with columns 'Auslage / Porto / Franko'.

(a) Top lines, mostly struck out. Riemann is setting up the local description of singularities. An algebraic function behaves near a point of T, including a branch point, in a known way. This follows from the 'known theorems on the expansion of a function', expanded in powers of the local parameter, as the next page makes explicit. A logarithmic singularity a·log(...) can be made continuous at that point by subtracting a suitable expression; the struck word 'a log' survives.

(b) Periodicity moduli. Let α+βi be the function constructed on the previous page on the dissected surface T'. It has the prescribed singular parts (a_ν log t + b_ν/t + c_ν/t² + …) at the points ε_ν. It jumps by 2πi·a_ν across the lines l_ν and by constants across the 2p cross-cuts. The constants k^(1), …, k^(2p) by which it is larger on the positive side of the cross-cuts are called its Periodicitätsmoduln.

(c) Dirichlet principle. By adding a function γ(x,y), continuous everywhere on T' with purely imaginary periodicity moduli, α+βi can be turned into a function ω of x+yi. That ω is determined up to an additive constant.
- Hence ω has the same discontinuities in T as α+βi, and the same real parts of its moduli.
- Since these data were arbitrary, a holomorphic multivalued function on T is fixed, up to a constant, by its singular parts and the real parts of its 2p moduli. Only the imaginary parts of the moduli are then determined.
- Riemann adds: 'It will be shown that this function ω contains all [the relevant functions] as special cases.'

(d) Classification:
- I. Functions that stay finite everywhere: integrals of the first kind.
- II. Functions that become infinite (algebraically) at single points of the surface: integrals of the second kind.
- III. Functions that become logarithmically infinite at two points of the surface: integrals of the third kind.

(e) Integrals of the first kind. Let w_1, …, w_p be everywhere-finite such functions. Then w = α_1 w_1 + … + α_p w_p + const, with constant α_μ, is also one. Write k_μ^(ν) for the modulus of w_μ at the ν-th cross-cut. The modulus of w is then
  k^(ν) = Σ_μ α_μ k_μ^(ν).
Put α_μ = γ_μ + iδ_μ. Then
  Re k^(ν) = Σ_μ (γ_μ Re k_μ^(ν) − δ_μ Im k_μ^(ν)).
So the real parts of the 2p moduli are real-linear functions of the 2p reals γ_1..γ_p, δ_1..δ_p.

The page is fragmentary here; the following completion is mine, but certain from the next page and the published text. Suppose w_1..w_p satisfy no linear relation with constant coefficients. Then the 2p×2p real determinant is non-zero. Otherwise some non-trivial w would have all real parts zero, i.e. purely imaginary moduli and no singularities. By the uniqueness half of the Dirichlet principle such a w is constant, contradicting independence. Therefore the γ, δ can be chosen to give arbitrary real parts of the moduli. Consequently every everywhere-finite function equals Σ α_μ w_μ + const.

The next page continues: no further independent w_{p+1} exists; then Class II, functions with a pole b/(z−s).
errors: No mathematical errors are visible in the legible portions. The uniqueness argument (purely imaginary moduli and no singularities imply constant) is the standard Riemann/Dirichlet argument. It is rigorous modulo the Dirichlet principle itself, whose justification was later criticised by Weierstrass.
The existence of p independent first-kind integrals is assumed here rather than proved on this page; the published text derives it from the Dirichlet construction.

results.what: Existence and uniqueness (up to an additive constant) of a multivalued holomorphic function on a Riemann surface with prescribed singular parts and prescribed real parts of its periods, via the Dirichlet principle
results.modern_name: Riemann existence theorem for abelian integrals / normalization by real parts of periods

results.what: Classification of abelian integrals into first, second and third kind (finite everywhere; algebraic poles; logarithmic singularities at two points)
results.modern_name: Abelian differentials of the first, second, third kind
results.usually_credited_to: Legendre/Abel (kinds); Riemann 1857 for the surface-theoretic formulation

results.what: Integrals of the first kind form a p-dimensional complex space; the real parts of the 2p periods are real-linearly independent coordinates, with a non-singular 2p×2p real matrix
results.modern_name: Dimension of holomorphic differentials = genus; periods span a lattice (Jacobian non-degeneracy)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of §§3–5 of Riemann's published 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'; content matches the published text. Only the draft wording and the use of a printed postal form are of minor archival interest.

checkable.asserts: Re((γ+iδ)k) = γ Re k − δ Im k, so real parts of the moduli are real-linear in γ, δ (should give 0)
Genus 1 with periods 1, τ=t1+i t2: the real-part matrix has determinant −Im τ ≠ 0, so arbitrary real parts of the periods are attainable

transcription_corrections: Top line: 'den bekannten Nöthigen' is more likely 'den bekannten Sätzen über die Entwicklung einer Function'; the next page has 'Nach bekannten Sätzen über die Entwicklung einer Function in Potenzreihen'.
'durch Hinzufügung einer [-Function-] γ allenthalben stetigen Function' should read 'durch Hinzufügung einer allenthalben stetigen Function'; the 'γ' is likely a misreading or a struck letter.
'[-der periodischen-] Reihe [-Function-]' is probably 'Periodicitätsmoduln der Function'; 'Reihe' is doubtful.
The page is written on a printed form headed 'No 10.' with column headings 'Auslage', 'Porto', 'Franko'; these are not part of Riemann's text.
Label for class II reads 'in einzelnen Punkten der Fläche'; for class III 'in zwei Punkten der Fläche logarithmisch unendlich werden'.
